title: Delhi
selection: Delhi recorded an estimated 1.999 million foreign tourist visits in 2024 (India Tourism Data Compendium 2025, Table 4.1.2) and is the busiest international gateway for arrivals from Europe and the Americas. It has three UNESCO World Heritage Sites; Qutub Minar (220,044), Humayun's Tomb (158,043) and Red Fort (79,311) are among the ten ASI monuments most visited by foreign visitors in FY 2024-25 (Table 4.2.2). v2 (2026-11-05): key facts, regions and shopping added to the state record, and 10 neighbourhood pages, from Incredible India, Delhi Tourism (DTTDC) and Wikipedia. Delhi Tourism's 'About' page predates several projects it calls under construction, so only its lasting facts are used. No prices are given.

D1.claim: Delhi has three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Red Fort, Qutub Minar and Humayun's Tomb.

evidence.quote: Delhi’s skyline is adorned with three incredible UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

D2.claim: The Ministry of Tourism recommends the cooler months, October to March, for exploring Delhi.

evidence.quote: Delhi's magic unfolds in the cooler months (from October to March) when the weather is perfect for exploring

D3.claim: Delhi has very hot summers, peaking in late May or early June, and mild winters with dense fog.

evidence.quote: This features very hot summers accompanied by frequent thunderstorms locally known as andhi , and mild winters that are characterized by dense fog .
Summer starts in early April and peaks in late May or early June

D4.claim: The monsoon reaches Delhi in late June and lasts until mid-September.

evidence.quote: the summer monsoon entering in late June and continuing till mid-September

D5.claim: Delhi was the world's most polluted capital city in the World Air Quality Report 2024; crop-residue burning in neighbouring states worsens the smog.

evidence.quote: According to the World Air Quality Report 2024, Delhi remains the world's most polluted capital city.
burning of agricultural waste in nearby Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh regions results in severe intensification of smog over Delhi

D6.claim: Delhi has been built, destroyed and rebuilt several times and is home to eight historic cities.

evidence.quote: Home to eight historic cities, this ancient city has been built, destroyed, and rebuilt several times

D7.claim: Indira Gandhi International Airport has been India's busiest airport by passenger traffic since 2009.

evidence.quote: it is the busiest airport of India in terms of passenger traffic since 2009.

D8.claim: The Airport Express metro line links the airport with New Delhi station, a journey of about 15 minutes.

evidence.quote: linking Indira Gandhi International Airport to the commuter network.
providing for a 15-minute journey from New Delhi to IGI Airport

D9.claim: Delhi's five main railway stations are New Delhi, Old Delhi, Hazrat Nizamuddin, Anand Vihar Terminal and Sarai Rohilla.

evidence.quote: Along with Old Delhi railway station , Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station , Anand Vihar Terminal , and Sarai Rohilla Railway Station , it is one of the five primary railway stations catering to Delhi state

D10.claim: New Delhi railway station is next to Paharganj, about 2 km north of Connaught Place.

evidence.quote: right next to Paharganj , approximately 2 kilometers north of Connaught Place

D11.topic: Getting around: metro and cycle rickshaws
D11.claim: The Delhi Metro connects the city and nearby areas; cycle rickshaws are a good way to explore Old Delhi's narrow lanes.

evidence.quote: Hop on the swanky Delhi Metro, a clean and efficient lifeline connecting the city and nearby areas.
Navigating the narrow lanes on a cycle rickshaw is a fun and authentic way to soak up the atmosphere.

D12.claim: The first coach of every Delhi Metro train is reserved for women.

evidence.quote: Since October 2010, the first coach of every train is reserved for women

D13.claim: Delhi's classic dishes include butter chicken, dal makhani, chaat, dahi bhalla, chole bhature and jalebi; Mughlai cuisine originated here.

evidence.quote: The city's classic dishes include butter chicken , dal makhani , shahi paneer , aloo chaat , chaat , dahi bhalla
is where Mughlai cuisine originated

D14.claim: Chandni Chowk, the heart of Old Delhi, is the place for spices, sweets and street food.

evidence.quote: the heart of Old Delhi, for a sensory overload of spices, sweets, and street food.

D15.claim: Popular markets include Connaught Place, Chandni Chowk, Lajpat Nagar, Khan Market and Sarojini Nagar; Dilli Haat sells handicrafts from across India.

evidence.quote: Experience the city like a local by browsing vibrant markets like Connaught Place, Chandni Chowk, Lajpat Nagar, Khan Market, and Sarojini Nagar.
beckons souvenir hunters with its curated collection of handicrafts and regional specialities

D16.claim: 112 is India's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.

evidence.quote: 112 is now the pan-country single emergency number for all emergencies.

D17.claim: e-Tourist visa applications should be made at least 4 days before arrival, with a passport valid for at least six months.

evidence.quote: For e-Tourist and e-Business visa, Applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance of the date of arrival.
Applicant's passport should have at least six months validity at the time of making application for grant of e-Visa.

D18.claim: International visitors can pay by QR code using NPCI's UPI One World wallet, set up after a passport-and-visa KYC check.

evidence.quote: The UPI One World wallet can be availed through authorized PPI issuers at airports, hotels, designated money exchange locations and other touchpoints, following a full KYC process based on a passport and valid visa.

R1.claim: Shah Jahan ordered the Red Fort built in 1639 when he moved his court from Agra to Delhi; it was the Mughal emperors' residence for almost 200 years.

evidence.quote: In 1639, Shah Jahan decided to move his court from Agra to Delhi and ordered the Red Fort to be built as his majestic new home.
It served as the residence of Mughal emperors for almost 200 years!

R2.claim: The Red Fort Complex became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.

evidence.quote: The Red Fort, as part of the Red Fort Complex, was recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.

R3.claim: The Red Fort is open 9:30 am to 4:30 pm and closed on Mondays.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09:30 AM - 04:30 PM (Closed on Mondays)

R4.claim: Visits begin at the Lahori Gate and pass through the covered Meena Bazaar (Chhatta Chowk).

evidence.quote: Your journey begins at the Lahori Gate, the grand entryway named after its orientation towards Lahore.
explore the bustling Meena Bazaar (or Chhatta Chowk)

R5.claim: The Mumtaz Mahal houses the Red Fort Archaeological Museum, and the Naubat Khana's upper floor houses the Indian War Memorial Museum.

evidence.quote: The Mumtaz Mahal now houses the Red Fort Archaeological Museum.
Today, its upper floor houses the Indian War Memorial Museum.

R6.claim: A sound and light show runs every evening except Mondays.

evidence.quote: Every evening (except Mondays), this captivating spectacle brings the Red Fort's story to life

R7.claim: Every Independence Day (15 August) the Prime Minister raises the national flag at the Red Fort.

evidence.quote: Every year on Independence Day (August 15th), the Prime Minister raises the national flag at the Red Fort and addresses the nation from within its grounds.

R8.claim: The Red Fort was the fourth most visited ticketed ASI monument for domestic visitors in 2024–25, with 2,884,399 visits.

evidence.quote: Red Fort 2884399 5.32 4 Humayuns Tomb 158043 6.54

Q1.claim: The Qutub Minar is a 72.5 m red and buff sandstone tower from the 12th century, the tallest masonry tower in India.

evidence.quote: Standing at 72.5 meters (237.8 feet), this masterpiece is the tallest masonry tower in India.
The monument, constructed from red and buff sandstone in the 12th century, has withstood the test of time.

Q2.claim: Qutb-ud-din Aibak began the tower in 1199 and built the first storey; his successor Iltutmish added three more.

evidence.quote: It began in 1199 when Qutb-ud-din Aibak, a leader under Muhammad of Ghor, laid its foundation
Aibak's successor, Shamsuddin Iltutmish, continued the project by adding three more storeys.

Q3.claim: The Qutb complex was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1993.

evidence.quote: It was added to the list of World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1993.

Q4.claim: The complex also includes the Quwwat ul-Islam Mosque, the Alai Darwaza, the unfinished Alai Minar, the Iron Pillar and the tombs of Iltutmish and Alauddin Khalji.

evidence.quote: including the majestic Quwwat ul-Islam Mosque, the impressive Alai Darwaza gate, the intriguing Alai Minar, and the enigmatic Iron Pillar
you'll discover the tombs of prominent figures like Iltutmish, Alauddin Khalji, and Imam Zamin

Q5.claim: The Iron Pillar carries a 4th-century Sanskrit inscription in Brahmi script.

evidence.quote: The Iron Pillar in the courtyard bears an inscription in Sanskrit in Brahmi script of fourth century A.D.

Q6.claim: The Qutub Minar is open from sunrise to sunset; timings may vary with the season.

evidence.quote: Opening time - Sunrise to sunset, may vary seasonally.

Q7.claim: In 2024 the Qutub Minar was India's third most visited ticketed monument for both domestic (3.20 million) and foreign (0.22 million) visitors.

evidence.quote: followed by Sun Temple, Konark (3.57 million) and Qutub Minar, Delhi (3.20 million).
followed by Agra Fort (0.22 million) and Qutub Minar, Delhi (0.22 million).

H1.claim: Humayun's Tomb was commissioned in 1558 by Empress Bega Begum, Humayun's first wife, and designed by Persian architects.

evidence.quote: Commissioned in 1558 by Empress Bega Begum, Humayun's first wife and chief consort

H2.topic: First garden tomb and Taj Mahal forerunner
H2.claim: It was the first garden tomb on the Indian subcontinent and a major inspiration for the Taj Mahal.

evidence.quote: the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent
This pioneering design served as a major inspiration for future architectural innovations, culminating in the breathtaking wonder—the Taj Mahal.

H3.claim: Humayun's Tomb was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

evidence.quote: The tomb was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993

H4.claim: Over 100 graves of the Mughal dynasty lie within the complex, which also holds Isa Khan's tomb and the Nila Gumbad.

evidence.quote: with over 100 graves housed within its grounds
Isa Khan's Tomb, pre-dating Humayun's itself

H5.claim: The tomb is in Nizamuddin East near Purana Qila; the Nizamuddin Dargah and Sunder Nursery are a short walk away.

evidence.quote: Located in Nizamuddin East, close to the Purana Qila (Old Fort)
A short walk away, find tranquillity at the Nizamuddin Dargah

H6.claim: Humayun's Tomb is open from sunrise to sunset.

evidence.quote: Opening time - From sunrise to sunset

H7.claim: Humayun's Tomb received 158,043 foreign visitors in 2024–25, the fourth highest of any ticketed ASI monument.

evidence.quote: Red Fort 2884399 5.32 4 Humayuns Tomb 158043 6.54

J1.claim: Shah Jahan built the Jama Masjid between 1650 and 1656 at the highest point of Shahjahanabad; it is one of India's largest mosques.

evidence.quote: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Jama Masjid between 1650 and 1656, at the highest point of Shahjahanabad.
is one of the largest mosques in India

J2.claim: The courtyard can hold up to 25,000 worshippers.

evidence.quote: featuring a vast courtyard that can hold up to 25,000 worshipers

J3.claim: The Jama Masjid is open 7 am–12 pm and 1:30 pm–6:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 07:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 01:30 PM - 06:30 PM

J4.claim: Visitors can climb the southern minaret for views over Old Delhi.

evidence.quote: For an unforgettable experience, climb its southern minaret and gaze across Old Delhi where its history unfolds before your very eyes!

C1.claim: Chandni Chowk was laid out in the 17th century by Shah Jahan when he moved his capital to Delhi; the name means 'Moonlight Square'.

evidence.quote: Chandni Chowk, built in the 17th century, was a brainchild of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
The name “Chandni Chowk” translates to “Moonlight Square,”

C2.topic: Khari Baoli spice market and Dariba Kalan
C2.claim: Khari Baoli is Asia's largest wholesale spice market, and Dariba Kalan is known for jewellery and ittar (natural perfume).

evidence.quote: Inhale the intoxicating aromas of Khari Baoli, Asia's largest wholesale spice market
Dariba Kalan, once known as "Jeweller's Street," awaits with gleaming pearls, captivating natural perfumes (ittars)

C3.claim: Chandni Chowk is known for Mughlai restaurants and street food.

evidence.quote: from the famous Mughlai cuisine food joints to local street food, the food here is an adventure.

G1.claim: India Gate is a 42 m sandstone arch designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens as a memorial to 70,000 Indian soldiers who died in the First World War and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.

evidence.quote: India Gate, an awe-inspiring 42-meter-high archway of sandstone
it's a poignant memorial to the 70,000 Indian soldiers who laid down their lives during World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War

G2.claim: The foundation stone was laid in 1921 and the monument was dedicated in 1931.

evidence.quote: a path that began in 1921 when the Duke of Connaught laid its foundation stone
Lord Irwin, the then Viceroy, dedicated it to the nation in 1931

G3.claim: India Gate is open throughout the day, though some areas are closed after dark.

evidence.quote: Open throughout the day (Some areas are not accessible to visitors after dark).

G4.claim: The National War Memorial is a short walk away, and the National Gallery of Modern Art is nearby.

evidence.quote: You can begin with a short walk to the National War Memorial

L1.claim: The Lotus Temple is a Bahá'í House of Worship, opened in December 1986 and open to people of all religions.

evidence.quote: opened to the public for worship in December 1986
Anyone may enter the Lotus Temple regardless of religion, ethnicity or gender

L2.claim: The temple has 27 free-standing marble petals in clusters of three, nine doors and a hall for 2,500 people.

evidence.quote: Composed of 27 free-standing marble petals arranged into clusters of three, nine doors lead to its central hall which can accommodate up to 2,500 people

L3.claim: The Lotus Temple is open 9:30 am–7 pm in summer and 9:30 am–5:30 pm in winter.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09:30 AM - 07:00 PM (Summers)
09:30 AM - 05:30 PM (Winters)

L4.claim: Programmes in the prayer hall are readings from the sacred texts of many religions; at other times visitors may pray or meditate in silence.

evidence.quote: at certain times members of the public may meditate and pray in silence

K1.claim: Akshardham is open 9:30 am–6:30 pm, Tuesday to Sunday, and closed on Mondays.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09:30 AM - 06:30 PM (Tuesday-Sunday)
Closed on Mondays

K2.claim: Visitors must leave all electronic devices, including phones and cameras, at designated areas before entering.

evidence.quote: Visitors are kindly requested to leave all electronic devices, including cameras and mobile phones, at designated areas before entering.

K3.claim: The complex is about half a kilometre from Akshardham metro station.

evidence.quote: Conveniently located just half a kilometre from the Akshardham metro station

K4.claim: The temple, built of Carrara marble and pink sandstone, is dedicated to Bhagwan Swaminarayan; the complex also has a boat ride, the Hall of Values and an evening water show.

evidence.quote: Crafted from gleaming Italian Carrara marble and warm pink sandstone
As day turns to night, the Sahaj Anand Water Show presents a mesmerizing spectacle at the temple's traditional step well.

B1.claim: The gurdwara stands on the site of Raja Jai Singh's palace, where the eighth Sikh Guru, Guru Har Krishan, stayed in 1664 and helped the sick during an epidemic.

evidence.quote: In 1664, the eighth Sikh Guru, Sri Guru Har Krishan Ji visited Delhi and resided at this very palace.
Guru Har Krishan Ji responded by offering aid to the suffering

B2.claim: Volunteers serve free meals (langar) to thousands of people every day, regardless of caste, creed or status.

evidence.quote: volunteers tirelessly prepare and serve free meals to thousands daily, regardless of caste, creed, or social status

B3.claim: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib is open 24 hours a day.

evidence.quote: Open 24X7

G5.topic: Republic Day parade on Kartavya Path
G5.claim: The Republic Day parade is held along Kartavya Path, beside India Gate, every 26 January.

evidence.quote: Every January 26, a grand parade is held along Kartavya Path (earlier known as Rajpath)

DS1.claim: Delhi's wider urban area — with Gurgaon, Noida, Ghaziabad and Faridabad in the National Capital Region — has over 28 million people, India's largest metropolitan area.

evidence.quote: has an estimated population of over 28 million, making it the largest metropolitan area in India and the fourth-largest in the world

DS2.claim: Delhi's air is usually satisfactory to moderate from March to September and poor to hazardous from October to February; stubble burning in Punjab and Haryana adds to it in October.

evidence.quote: The air quality index (AQI) in Delhi generally falls within the Satisfactory (51–100) and Moderate (101–200) ranges between March and September, and then drastically deteriorates to Poor (201–300), Severe (301–400), or Hazardous (401–500+) levels between October and February
the air quality drastically deteriorated in October, the season of crop burning in Punjab and Haryana

DS3.claim: Indira Gandhi International Airport is at Palam, about 15 km south-west of New Delhi station.

evidence.quote: is situated in Palam , Delhi , 15 km (9.

DS4.claim: Noida International Airport at Jewar, in Uttar Pradesh, opened its first phase on 28 March 2026.

evidence.quote: The first phase was inaugurated on 28 March 2026

DS7.claim: Dilli Haat, opened in 1994, has three sites — opposite INA market, Pitampura and Janakpuri — where craft stalls from different states rotate.

evidence.quote: Established in 1994
The most prominent one is opposite the iconic INA market, another is in Pitampura, and the third one is in Janakpuri.
the ever-changing showcase of arts and crafts shops, which rotate periodically

OD1.claim: Old Delhi is Shahjahanabad, Shah Jahan's walled capital of 1648, which stayed the Mughal capital until 1857; the Red Fort, Jama Masjid and the Digambar Jain Lal Mandir are its landmarks.

evidence.quote: officially named Shahjahanabad in 1648, upon Shah Jahan 's decision to shift the imperial Mughal capital from Agra
it remained the capital of Mughal India until its fall in 1857
The major landmark monuments built during the Mughal era are the Red Fort , now a UNESCO World Heritage Site , the Jama Masjid , and the Sri Digambar Jain Lal Mandir .

OD2.claim: Today it is known for its bazaars, restaurants and street food.

evidence.quote: is renowned for its bustling bazaars , restaurants , street food

OD3.claim: Raj Ghat, by the Yamuna, is the black-marble memorial where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated on 31 January 1948, with an eternal flame.

evidence.quote: marked Mahatma Gandhi's Antyeshti (last rites), held on 31 January 1948
admire the eternal flame that commemorates Gandhi's legacy

OD4.claim: Feroz Shah Kotla, the 14th-century citadel of Firozabad, holds an Ashokan pillar brought from Topra and the Tughlaq Jami Masjid.

evidence.quote: Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq built this impressive fortress in the 14th century
A marvel not to be missed is the Topra Ashokan Pillar of polished sandstone.

CP1.claim: Connaught Place (Rajiv Chowk), built 1929–1933 to Robert Tor Russell's design, is New Delhi's main business, shopping and nightlife hub.

evidence.quote: Connaught Place , also known as Rajiv Chowk, is one of the main financial, commercial and business centres in New Delhi
It houses the headquarters of several noted Indian firms and is a major shopping, nightlife, and tourist destination in New Delhi.
it saw construction begin in 1929 and was completed in 1933. It was designed by Robert Tor Russell .

CP2.claim: Agrasen ki Baoli on Hailey Road, a short walk away, is a 60-m stepwell with 108 steps, probably repaired in the Tughlaq or Lodi era.

evidence.quote: this 60 metres long and 15 metres wide ancient stepwell with 108 steps
This baoli was probably repaired during the Tughlaq or Lodi eras

LD1.claim: Lutyens' Delhi, built from the late 1910s to the 1930s, is the British-era capital designed largely by Edwin Lutyens, laid out on a ceremonial axis — today Kartavya Path — ending at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

evidence.quote: Work lasted between the late-1910s and 1930s.
Lutyens conceived of a modern imperial city centred around a "ceremonial axis"
Finally it ends at the gates of Rashtrapati Bhavan.

LD2.claim: The National Museum holds over 200,000 works, including the 4,500-year-old Dancing Girl of Harappa.

evidence.quote: houses over 200,000 mesmerising artworks, sculptures, and manuscripts
The famous Dancing Girl of Harappa, a 4,500-year-old bronze statue

LD3.claim: Purana Qila, on Mathura Road, is the 16th-century citadel of Humayun's Dinpanah, with walls nearly 1.5 km long and finds from 1000 BC in its museum.

evidence.quote: This 16th-century marvel served as the inner citadel of Dinpanah, the sixth city of Delhi.
Its towering walls, which stretch nearly 1.5 kilometres and reach 18 meters in height
The collection features Painted Grey Ware from 1000 BC

NZ1.claim: The Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah, shrine of the 13th-century Sufi saint, draws thousands every week and is known for its evening qawwali; Amir Khusrau is buried at its entrance.

evidence.quote: is visited by thousands of pilgrims every week
The site is also known for its evening qawwali devotional music sessions.
The tombs of Amir Khusrau , Nizamuddin's disciple, and Jehan Ara Begum , Shah Jahan 's daughter, are located at the entrance to the complex.

NZ2.claim: Sunder Nursery, a 90-acre Mughal-era garden beside Humayun's Tomb, reopened as a heritage park in 2018 with 15 monuments and over 300 kinds of trees.

evidence.quote: is spread over 90 acres (36 hectare)
Today Sunder Nursery contains fifteen heritage monuments
the nursery reopened to public as a heritage park on 21 February 2018. Now it contains over 300 types of trees

NZ3.claim: Nizamuddin West sits amid Humayun's Tomb, Sunder Nursery and the Delhi Golf Club, near Khan Market and Lodhi Garden.

evidence.quote: It sits in the green lung of Delhi, with Humayun's Tomb , Sunder Nursery and Delhi Golf club around it.

LR1.claim: Lodi Gardens, 90 acres between Khan Market and Safdarjung's Tomb, holds 15th–16th-century Sayyid and Lodi tombs — Muhammad Shah's, Sikandar Lodi's, the Bara and Shisha Gumbad — and is a favourite for morning walks.

evidence.quote: Spread over 90 acres
it contains Muhammad Shah 's tomb, the tomb of Sikandar Lodi , the Shisha Gumbad and the Bara Gumbad
The gardens are situated between Khan Market and Safdarjung's Tomb on Lodi Road and are a popular spot for morning walks for Delhiites.

LR2.claim: The garden was landscaped in 1936 as Lady Willingdon Park and renamed after independence; Joseph Allen Stein and Garrett Eckbo added a glass house, lake and bonsai park in 1968.

evidence.quote: In 1936, during British colonial rule, Lady Willingdon redesigned the area
Post-independence in 1947, it was renamed Lodhi Garden.
who added a glass house, a fountain-adorned lake, and specialist sections like the bonsai park and rose garden

LR3.claim: Khan Market was set up in 1951 for refugees from the North-West Frontier Province after Partition.

evidence.quote: It was established in 1951 by the newly constituted Republic of India 's Rehabilitation Ministry to give economic opportunities to refugees of the Partition of India

LR4.claim: The India Habitat Centre hosts cultural events nearby.

evidence.quote: The nearby India Habitat Centre hosts cultural events and exhibitions.

HK1.claim: Hauz Khas — 'royal tank' — is named after the reservoir Alauddin Khalji built to supply Siri Fort; it now has hostels, cafes and the Deer Park.

evidence.quote: giving it the meaning of 'royal tank'
was first built by Alauddin Khalji (r. 1296–1316)
The area attracts young tourists with numerous hostels and cafes .
Hauz Khas has some of the largest green areas in Delhi, namely Deer Park and Rose garden .

HK2.claim: Easy metro access makes it a popular base for visitors.

evidence.quote: has easy access to the Delhi Metro , making it a preferred location for many visitors to India

HK3.claim: Known earlier as Hauz-e-Alai, it is where Ghazi Malik defeated Khusro Khan in 1320.

evidence.quote: Historically Hauz Khas was known as Hauz-e-Alai and is the place where Khusro Khan of Delhi Sultanate was defeated by Ghazi Malik (Governor of Dipalpur) in 1320.

MT2.claim: The gurdwara is one of the oldest Sikh shrines in Delhi, on an estate donated by Ranjit Singh.

evidence.quote: Today it is one of oldest extant Sikh shrines in Delhi and the surrounding estate of donated by early 19th-century Sikh emperor, Ranjit Singh .

MH1.claim: Mehrauli is held to be Delhi's oldest continuously inhabited village, founded by the Tomars; it was the capital of the first Delhi Sultanate.

evidence.quote: Mehrauli village is considered the oldest continuously inhabited village in Delhi and is founded by the Tomar Rajputs in 1060 A.D
Mehrauli remained the capital of the Mamluk dynasty which ruled until 1290.

MH2.claim: The 200-acre Mehrauli Archaeological Park beside the Qutub Minar has over 50 monuments, including Balban's tomb with India's first true arch, Jamali Kamali and Rajon ki Baoli.

evidence.quote: a 200-acre treasure trove nestled in the heart of South Delhi
this remarkable park houses over 50 historically significant monuments
featuring the country's first true arch and dome
the 16th-century Rajon Ki Baoli, or Stepwell of the Masons

MH3.claim: The dargah of Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki here hosts the annual Phoolwalon-ki-Sair festival.

evidence.quote: is also situated near the Qutub Minar Complex and the venue for the annual Phoolwalon-ki-sair Festival

PG1.claim: Paharganj, just west of New Delhi station, is full of budget hotels and cafes, but has a poor record for women's safety, scams and drugs.

evidence.quote: located just west of the New Delhi Railway Station
Known for its concentration of affordable hotels, lodges, restaurants, dhabas , and a wide variety of shops
However, Paharganj has a poor record regarding the safety of women since the area is noted for its scams, drug peddling, sexual assaults.

MT1.claim: Majnu-ka-Tilla, on the Yamuna, grew from a 1960 Tibetan refugee camp and is still home to Tibetan families; its gurdwara marks where Guru Nanak met the Sufi Majnu in 1505.

evidence.quote: The land was allotted by the Government of India to the refugees in 1960.
Today, it is home to second generation of Tibet refugees and is also known as Samyeling
met first Sikh Guru , Guru Nanak Dev Ji on 20 July 1505

AE1.claim: Aerocity, part of the airport, is a hospitality district of hotels on the Airport Express metro line, between Delhi and Gurgaon.

evidence.quote: ultimately housing 16 luxury hotels and commercial spaces
The hospitality district of Aerocity offers quick access to the airport, besides being centrally located between the business areas of Delhi and Gurgaon .
The Delhi Aerocity metro station is located on the Delhi Airport Express Line of the Delhi Metro .

places.seoDescription: Plan your Delhi trip: Red Fort, Qutub Minar and Humayun's Tomb, Old Delhi food, metro and airport transfers, best season, air quality and practical tips.

images.caption: Humayun's Tomb, Delhi

overview.text:
India's capital is one of its oldest cities. The Ministry of Tourism counts eight historic cities within it, each built over the ruins of the last, and three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Shah Jahan's Red Fort, the 12th-century Qutub Minar and Humayun's Tomb, the garden mausoleum that inspired the Taj Mahal.

For most international travellers Delhi is also the start of the trip: Indira Gandhi International has been India's busiest airport since 2009, and the city is the first stop on the classic Golden Triangle with Agra and Jaipur. Give it at least two days. Spend one in Old Delhi — the Red Fort, the Jama Masjid and the lanes of Chandni Chowk — and one in New Delhi and the south, from Humayun's Tomb and India Gate to the Qutub complex.

Timing matters here more than in most cities. October to March is the comfortable season, summers are very hot, and winter brings fog and, often, heavy smog. Several big sights close one day a week, so check the visiting information below before you fix your days.

items.body: Red Fort: Shah Jahan's palace-fortress, home to the Mughal emperors for almost 200 years (closed Mondays).
Qutub Minar: the 72.5 m tower begun in 1199, surrounded by the ruins of Delhi's first mosque.
Humayun's Tomb: the first garden tomb on the subcontinent, and the model for the Taj Mahal.
Chandni Chowk: Old Delhi's spice markets, jewellers' lanes and street food.
Gurudwara Bangla Sahib: free langar served to thousands every day, open around the clock.
Spend a day in Old Delhi: the Red Fort, the Jama Masjid's southern minaret and the spice market at Khari Baoli.
See the Mughal and Sultanate monuments: Humayun's Tomb in the morning and the Qutub complex in the late afternoon.
Shop the markets — Connaught Place, Chandni Chowk, Lajpat Nagar, Khan Market and Sarojini Nagar — or buy crafts from across India at Dilli Haat.
Eat your way through Chandni Chowk's street food and sweets.
Watch the evening sound and light show at the Red Fort (not on Mondays).

best_time.text:
October to March is the season the Ministry of Tourism recommends, and it is the most comfortable time for walking around monuments. Summer starts in April and peaks in late May or early June, when heat waves are common. The monsoon arrives in late June and lasts until mid-September.

Winter has its own catch. Dense fog is common, and in the World Air Quality Report 2024 Delhi was the world's most polluted capital, with smog made worse by crop burning in neighbouring states. If you are sensitive to air pollution, check the daily air-quality index before planning a day outdoors, and consider November and December the riskiest months.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Indira Gandhi International Airport is India's busiest and the main gateway for international visitors. The Airport Express metro line runs from the airport to New Delhi station in about 15 minutes.

By train: Delhi has five main stations — New Delhi, Old Delhi, Hazrat Nizamuddin, Anand Vihar Terminal and Sarai Rohilla. Check which one your train uses. New Delhi station sits next to Paharganj, about 2 km north of Connaught Place. Book tickets on IRCTC.

local_transport.text: The Delhi Metro is the easiest way to cover long distances: it connects most of the city and nearby towns, and the first coach of every train is reserved for women. For Old Delhi, take the metro to the edge of the old city, then walk or hire a cycle rickshaw through the lanes. Auto-rickshaws and app-based taxis fill the gaps — agree the fare or use the meter before you set off.

where_to_stay.text: Paharganj, beside New Delhi station, is the traditional budget area and convenient for early trains. Connaught Place, about 2 km south, puts you at the centre of the metro network with plenty of restaurants. Many mid-range and upscale hotels are in South Delhi, which is calmer but further from Old Delhi. If you have an early flight, a hotel near the airport line saves time.

items.body: Delhi classics: butter chicken, dal makhani, chole bhature, dahi bhalla and chaat — Delhi is also where Mughlai cuisine originated.
Chandni Chowk for street food, sweets and spices — go hungry.
Langar (a free communal meal) at Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, open to everyone.
At mosques, temples and gurdwaras, dress modestly, remove your shoes and cover your head where asked (head scarves are usually provided at gurdwaras).
Akshardham doesn't allow phones or cameras inside — leave them at the cloakroom.
At the Lotus Temple, keep silence inside the prayer hall.
Ask before photographing people, especially at places of worship.

items.title: Emergency

items.title: Air quality
items.body: In winter, check the air-quality index daily; people with asthma or heart conditions should limit time outdoors on smoggy days.

items.title: Heat

items.title: Crowds

places.name: Red Fort
places.summary: Shah Jahan's red sandstone palace-fortress in Old Delhi, a World Heritage Site and home of the Mughal emperors for almost 200 years.
places.seoTitle: Red Fort Delhi: Timings, Monday Closure & What to See
places.seoDescription: Visit the Red Fort in Old Delhi: opening hours and Monday closure, the Lahori Gate, museums inside, the evening sound and light show and nearby sights.

images.commons: File:Lahori Gate, Red Fort, Delhi, India - September 2014.jpg
images.alt: The red sandstone walls and Lahori Gate of the Red Fort in Delhi under a blue sky
images.caption: Lahori Gate, Red Fort

overview.text:
In 1639 the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan moved his court from Agra to Delhi and ordered a new palace-fortress at the heart of his new city, Shahjahanabad. The Red Fort, named for its red sandstone walls, was the residence of the Mughal emperors for almost 200 years, and the Red Fort Complex became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.

Visits begin at the Lahori Gate and pass through the covered Meena Bazaar to the Naubat Khana, now the Indian War Memorial Museum, and on to the Diwan-i-Am and the marble pavilions of the private palaces. The Mumtaz Mahal houses the Red Fort Archaeological Museum. The fort still matters to modern India: every Independence Day the Prime Minister raises the national flag here. In 2024–25 it drew 2.88 million domestic visitors, the fourth most of any ticketed ASI monument.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: 9:30 am – 4:30 pm. Closed on Mondays.

items.title: Entrance
items.body: Through the Lahori Gate.

items.title: Sound and light show
items.body: Every evening except Mondays.

items.title: Tickets
items.body: Check the current fee on the Archaeological Survey of India's official site before you go.
Combine with the Jama Masjid and Chandni Chowk, all within walking distance.
Allow about two hours inside, more if you visit the museums.

places.name: Qutub Minar
places.summary: A 72.5 m sandstone tower begun in 1199, the tallest masonry tower in India, at the heart of a World Heritage complex in Mehrauli.
places.seoTitle: Qutub Minar Delhi: History, Timings & the Qutub Complex
places.seoDescription: Visit the Qutub Minar, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in south Delhi: the 12th-century tower, the Iron Pillar, Alai Darwaza, opening hours and tips.

images.alt: The Qutub Minar lit up at dusk beside a domed tomb in the Qutub complex, Delhi
images.caption: Qutub Minar at dusk

images.alt: Looking up at the fluted red sandstone storeys and balconies of the Qutub Minar
images.caption: The fluted storeys of the minar

overview.text:
Standing 72.5 m high, the Qutub Minar is the tallest masonry tower in India. Qutb-ud-din Aibak, founder of the Delhi Sultanate, began it in 1199 and completed the first storey; his successor Iltutmish added three more. Built of red and buff sandstone and covered in carved bands of inscriptions, it is the centrepiece of the Qutb complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993.

Give yourself time for the rest of the complex: the Quwwat ul-Islam Mosque, the Alai Darwaza gateway, the unfinished Alai Minar and the tombs of Iltutmish and Alauddin Khalji. In the courtyard, the Iron Pillar carries a 4th-century Sanskrit inscription in Brahmi script. In 2024 the Qutub Minar was India's third most visited ticketed monument for both Indian and foreign visitors.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: Sunrise to sunset; timings may vary with the season.

items.title: Tickets
items.body: Check the current fee on the Archaeological Survey of India's official site before you go.
Go in the late afternoon for warm light on the sandstone.
Allow 1.5–2 hours to see the whole complex, not just the tower.

places.name: Humayun's Tomb
places.summary: The first garden tomb on the Indian subcontinent, commissioned in 1558 — and the model for the Taj Mahal.
places.seoTitle: Humayun's Tomb Delhi: History, Timings & Visitor Tips
places.seoDescription: Visit Humayun's Tomb, the UNESCO-listed Mughal garden tomb in Nizamuddin, Delhi: history, opening hours, the tombs in the complex and nearby sights.

images.alt: Humayun's Tomb seen across its fountain and garden pool in Delhi
images.caption: Humayun's Tomb from the garden

overview.text:
Humayun's Tomb was commissioned in 1558 by Empress Bega Begum, Humayun's first wife, and built by Persian architects with Indian craftsmen. It was the first garden tomb on the Indian subcontinent, set in a four-part charbagh garden, and its design inspired later Mughal tombs, culminating in the Taj Mahal. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

The complex is sometimes called the necropolis of the Mughals: more than 100 graves lie within it. Before the main tomb you pass Isa Khan's tomb, which predates Humayun's, and the blue-tiled Nila Gumbad. The tomb is in Nizamuddin East, near Purana Qila, and the Nizamuddin Dargah and Sunder Nursery are a short walk away. In 2024–25 it received 158,043 foreign visitors, the fourth most of any ticketed ASI monument.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: Sunrise to sunset.

items.title: Tickets
items.body: Check the current fee on the Archaeological Survey of India's official site before you go.
Combine with Sunder Nursery next door and the qawwali at Nizamuddin Dargah.
Early morning is quietest and best for photographs.

places.name: Jama Masjid
places.summary: Shah Jahan's great mosque in Old Delhi, with a courtyard for 25,000 worshippers and minaret views over the old city.
places.seoTitle: Jama Masjid Delhi: Timings, Etiquette & Minaret Views
places.seoDescription: Visit the Jama Masjid in Old Delhi, one of India's largest mosques: history, visiting hours, dress and etiquette, and the climb up the southern minaret.

images.alt: The red sandstone courtyard and gateway of the Jama Masjid in Delhi with visitors
images.caption: The courtyard of the Jama Masjid

overview.text:
The Jama Masjid was built by Shah Jahan between 1650 and 1656 at the highest point of his new city, Shahjahanabad, and remains one of the largest mosques in India. Its red sandstone and marble courtyard can hold up to 25,000 worshippers, and it is still an active place of prayer.

For the best view of Old Delhi, climb the southern minaret. The mosque is a short walk from the Red Fort and the lanes of Chandni Chowk, so it fits easily into a day in the old city. Avoid prayer times, especially Friday midday prayers, when the mosque is busiest with worshippers.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: 7 am – 12 pm and 1:30 pm – 6:30 pm.

items.title: Dress
items.body: Cover shoulders and legs and remove your shoes before entering.
Visit after the Red Fort, then walk into Chandni Chowk for lunch.

places.name: Chandni Chowk
places.summary: Shah Jahan's 17th-century boulevard, now Old Delhi's busiest market: spices, jewellery, sweets and street food.
places.seoTitle: Chandni Chowk, Old Delhi: Markets & Street Food Guide
places.seoDescription: Explore Chandni Chowk in Old Delhi: Khari Baoli spice market, Dariba Kalan's jewellers, Mughlai food and street food, and how to get around the lanes.

images.commons: File:Chandni Chowk, Old Delhi, India - September 2014.jpg
images.alt: Rickshaws and traffic beside the Chandni Chowk street sign in Old Delhi
images.caption: Chandni Chowk, Old Delhi

overview.text:
Chandni Chowk was laid out in the 17th century by Shah Jahan as the grand boulevard of his new capital; its name means 'Moonlight Square', after a pool that once reflected the moon. Today it is the crowded, noisy heart of Old Delhi and one of the city's great experiences.

Each lane has its own trade. Khari Baoli is Asia's largest wholesale spice market; Dariba Kalan, once the street of jewellers, still sells silver, pearls and ittar (natural perfume). Food is the other reason to come — from long-established Mughlai restaurants to street food and sweets. Go with time and an appetite, and see it on foot or by cycle rickshaw.

items.body: Mornings are calmer; many shops open late morning.
Take the metro to the old city rather than driving — roads here are slow.
Keep bags closed and valuables out of sight in the crowds.

places.name: India Gate
places.summary: Lutyens's 42 m war memorial arch on Kartavya Path, a favourite place for an evening walk.
places.seoTitle: India Gate Delhi: History, Visiting Hours & Nearby Sights
places.seoDescription: Visit India Gate in New Delhi, the war memorial designed by Lutyens: its history, when to go, evening lights and nearby sights like the National War Memorial.

images.commons: File:India Gate, New Delhi from West.jpg
images.alt: The sandstone arch of India Gate seen across the lawns from the west, New Delhi
images.caption: India Gate from the west

overview.text:
India Gate is a 42 m sandstone arch designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens as a memorial to the 70,000 Indian soldiers who died in the First World War and the Third Anglo-Afghan War. The Duke of Connaught laid the foundation stone in 1921, and the Viceroy, Lord Irwin, dedicated it in 1931.

It stands on Kartavya Path, the ceremonial avenue where the Republic Day parade is held each January. The surrounding lawns are open all day and popular with families in the evening, when the arch is lit up, though some areas close after dark. The National War Memorial is a short walk away.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: Open throughout the day; some areas are closed to visitors after dark.

items.title: Entry
items.body: No ticket is needed to walk around the lawns.

places.name: Lotus Temple
places.summary: Delhi's Bahá'í House of Worship: 27 marble petals around a silent prayer hall open to people of every faith.
places.seoTitle: Lotus Temple Delhi: Timings, Etiquette & Architecture
places.seoDescription: Visit the Lotus Temple, Delhi's Bahá'í House of Worship: opening hours in summer and winter, silence in the prayer hall, and its 27-petal marble design.

images.alt: The white marble petals of the Lotus Temple above its blue reflecting pools in Delhi
images.caption: The Lotus Temple

overview.text:
The Lotus Temple is a Bahá'í House of Worship that opened in December 1986. As at every Bahá'í temple, anyone may enter regardless of religion. Its shape is unmistakable: 27 free-standing marble petals in clusters of three, with nine doors leading into a central hall for up to 2,500 people, surrounded by nine reflecting pools.

Inside there are no idols or sermons. At set times there are readings from the sacred texts of many faiths; at other times visitors may pray or meditate in silence. Expect a short queue at busy times, and keep your voice down in the hall.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: 9:30 am – 7 pm in summer; 9:30 am – 5:30 pm in winter.

items.title: Inside
items.body: Silence in the prayer hall; shoes are removed before entering.

places.seoTitle: Akshardham Temple Delhi: Timings, Rules & What to See
places.seoDescription: Visit Swaminarayan Akshardham in Delhi: opening hours and Monday closure, the no-phone rule, the boat ride, the evening water show and how to get there by metro.

overview.text: Swaminarayan Akshardham is a huge temple complex dedicated to Bhagwan Swaminarayan, built of Italian Carrara marble and pink sandstone. Beyond the temple itself there is a boat ride through Indian history, the Hall of Values exhibition and, after dark, the Sahaj Anand Water Show. It is about half a kilometre from Akshardham metro station. Phones and cameras are not allowed inside, and it is closed on Mondays.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: 9:30 am – 6:30 pm, Tuesday to Sunday. Closed on Mondays.

items.title: Electronics
items.body: Leave phones, cameras and other electronic devices at the designated area before entering.

items.title: Getting there
items.body: About 500 m from Akshardham metro station.

places.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
places.summary: Central Delhi's best-known Sikh gurdwara, with a sacred pool and a free community kitchen open to everyone.
places.seoTitle: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib Delhi: Langar, Etiquette & Timings
places.seoDescription: Visit Gurudwara Bangla Sahib in central Delhi: its history, the free langar served daily, the sarovar, etiquette for visitors and opening hours.

images.alt: The white gurdwara with a golden dome reflected in the sarovar at Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
images.caption: The sarovar at Gurudwara Bangla Sahib

overview.text:
Gurudwara Bangla Sahib stands on the site of a palace belonging to Raja Jai Singh, where the eighth Sikh Guru, Guru Har Krishan, stayed in 1664 and cared for the sick during an epidemic. Today its white marble building and golden domes rise above a large sarovar, or sacred pool.

The gurdwara welcomes visitors of every faith around the clock. In the langar hall, volunteers serve free meals to thousands of people every day, whatever their caste, creed or status — sitting down to eat together is the best way to understand the Sikh principle of equality. Cover your head, remove your shoes and wash your feet before entering.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: Open 24 hours.

items.title: Etiquette
items.body: Cover your head (scarves are available), remove your shoes and don't bring tobacco or alcohol.

overview.text:
Old Delhi is Shahjahanabad, the walled city Shah Jahan made his capital in 1648; it stayed the Mughal capital until 1857. The Red Fort, the Jama Masjid and the Digambar Jain Lal Mandir are its great landmarks, and Chandni Chowk, laid out in the 17th century, still runs through its heart.

Today it is known for bazaars and street food: Khari Baoli is Asia's largest wholesale spice market, and Dariba Kalan sells jewellery and ittar. Cycle rickshaws are the easiest way through the narrow lanes. By the Yamuna, Raj Ghat marks where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated in 1948, and Feroz Shah Kotla's ruins hold an Ashokan pillar.

Climb the Jama Masjid's southern minaret.

overview.text:
Connaught Place, officially Rajiv Chowk, was built between 1929 and 1933 to Robert Tor Russell's design as the showpiece commercial centre of New Delhi. Its white colonnaded circles are still the city's main hub for offices, shopping, restaurants and nightlife.

A short walk away on Hailey Road, Agrasen ki Baoli is a 60-m stepwell with 108 steps, probably repaired in the Tughlaq or Lodi era. New Delhi railway station is about 2 km north.

overview.text:
Lutyens' Delhi is the capital the British built from the late 1910s to the 1930s, largely to Edwin Lutyens's designs. Its spine is a ceremonial axis — today Kartavya Path — running from India Gate, the First World War memorial arch, up Raisina Hill to Rashtrapati Bhavan; the Republic Day parade marches along it every 26 January.

The National Museum, with over 200,000 works including the 4,500-year-old Dancing Girl of Harappa, is just off the avenue. Purana Qila, Humayun's 16th-century citadel, stands on Mathura Road.

overview.text:
Nizamuddin is named after the 13th-century Sufi saint whose dargah draws thousands of pilgrims every week; it is known for its evening qawwali, and the poet Amir Khusrau is buried at its entrance.

Around it lies Delhi's green lung. Humayun's Tomb, the first garden tomb in the subcontinent, is a short walk away, and next to it Sunder Nursery, a 90-acre Mughal-era garden, reopened in 2018 with 15 monuments and over 300 kinds of trees.

overview.text:
Lodi Gardens, 90 acres on Lodi Road between Khan Market and Safdarjung's Tomb, holds rare 15th- and 16th-century tombs of the Sayyid and Lodi dynasties — Muhammad Shah's, Sikandar Lodi's, the Bara Gumbad and the Shisha Gumbad — and is a favourite place for morning walks. It was landscaped in 1936 as Lady Willingdon Park and renamed after independence.

Khan Market, set up in 1951 for refugees from the North-West Frontier Province, is a short walk away, and the India Habitat Centre hosts cultural events nearby.

items.body: Walk Lodi Gardens early in the morning.
See the Bara Gumbad and Sikandar Lodi's tomb.
Browse Khan Market's bookshops and cafes.
Catch an event at the India Habitat Centre.

how_to_reach.text: Khan Market and JLN Stadium metro stations are nearby.

overview.text:
Hauz Khas — the 'royal tank' — is named after the reservoir Alauddin Khalji built to supply his city of Siri. The tank and its buildings are now the Hauz Khas Complex, ringed by some of Delhi's largest green spaces, the Deer Park and Rose Garden.

With easy metro access and plenty of hostels and cafes, it has become a popular base for young and budget travellers exploring South Delhi. Its history goes back further than the cafes suggest: known then as Hauz-e-Alai, it is where Ghazi Malik defeated Khusro Khan in 1320.

overview.text:
Mehrauli is held to be Delhi's oldest continuously inhabited village, founded by the Tomars, and it was the capital of the first Delhi Sultanate. The 72.5-m Qutub Minar, begun in 1199, rises above it.

Beside the minar, the 200-acre Mehrauli Archaeological Park holds more than 50 monuments: Balban's tomb, with India's first true arch and dome, the Jamali Kamali mosque and tomb, and Rajon ki Baoli, a 16th-century stepwell. The dargah of Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki hosts the annual Phoolwalon-ki-Sair festival.

items.body: See the Qutub Minar and the Iron Pillar.
Walk the Archaeological Park to Jamali Kamali and Rajon ki Baoli.
Visit the dargah of Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki.

how_to_reach.text: Qutub Minar metro station is close by; the Qutub complex is open sunrise to sunset.

overview.text:
Paharganj, just west of New Delhi railway station, is packed with budget hotels, lodges, dhabas and shops, and has long been the backpacker district. It is convenient for early trains.

It also has a poor record for women's safety and is known for scams and drug dealing, and many backpackers now base themselves in South Delhi instead. Connaught Place is about 2 km away.

items.title: Scams and safety
items.body: Paharganj is known for scams and drug dealing and has a poor record on women's safety — stay alert, especially at night.

how_to_reach.text: New Delhi railway station is next door; the Airport Express runs from there to the airport in about 15 minutes.

overview.text:
Majnu-ka-Tilla, on the banks of the Yamuna in north Delhi, grew from a Tibetan refugee camp on land the government allotted in 1960. Still home to Tibetan families, it is also called Samyeling, with a monastery, shops and cafes in its narrow lanes.

Its name comes from the Sufi Majnu, who ferried people across the river and met Guru Nanak here in 1505; the gurdwara that marks the spot is one of Delhi's oldest Sikh shrines, on an estate given by Ranjit Singh.

Visit the gurdwara.

overview.text:
Aerocity is the hospitality district of Indira Gandhi International Airport, planned for 16 luxury hotels and offices, with quick access to the terminals and a position between Delhi and Gurgaon.

Its station is on the Airport Express line, which reaches New Delhi station in about 15 minutes, so it suits travellers with early flights or a single night in transit.

The airport itself, at Palam about 15 km south-west of New Delhi station, has been India's busiest by passengers since 2009. A second airport, Noida International at Jewar in Uttar Pradesh, opened its first phase in March 2026 — check which one your flight uses.

how_to_reach.text: Delhi Aerocity station is on the Airport Express line; IGI airport is next door.

itineraries.title: Two days in Delhi: Old Delhi and the Mughal monuments
itineraries.summary: Day one in Old Delhi — the Red Fort, Jama Masjid and Chandni Chowk; day two from Humayun's Tomb to India Gate and the Qutub Minar.
itineraries.seoTitle: 2 Days in Delhi Itinerary: Old Delhi to Qutub Minar
itineraries.seoDescription: A realistic two-day Delhi itinerary: the Red Fort, Jama Masjid and Chandni Chowk, then Humayun's Tomb, India Gate and the Qutub Minar, with metro tips and timings.

plan.overview: Delhi is spread out and its traffic is slow, so this plan groups sights by area and uses the metro between them. Day 1 covers Old Delhi; Day 2 covers the Mughal and colonial monuments of New Delhi and the south. Don't start on a Monday: the Red Fort is closed that day — swap the days if you need to.

days.title: Old Delhi
days.summary: Shah Jahan's city: the fort, the great mosque and the market lanes between them.

stops.name: Red Fort
stops.note: Opens at 9:30 am; closed Mondays. Enter by the Lahori Gate.

stops.name: Jama Masjid
stops.note: Closed to visitors 12–1:30 pm; climb the southern minaret for the view.

stops.name: Chandni Chowk
stops.note: Lunch on Old Delhi food, then walk or take a cycle rickshaw to Khari Baoli and Dariba Kalan.

stops.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
stops.note: Open 24 hours; join the langar if you like.

days.travel: The Red Fort, Jama Masjid and Chandni Chowk are within walking distance of each other. Take a metro or taxi to Bangla Sahib in central Delhi.
days.meals: Street food or a Mughlai lunch in Chandni Chowk; langar at Bangla Sahib.

days.title: New Delhi and the Qutub Minar
days.summary: From the first Mughal garden tomb to the Delhi Sultanate's victory tower.

stops.name: Humayun's Tomb
stops.note: Opens at sunrise; mornings are quietest.

stops.name: India Gate
stops.note: Walk the lawns; the National War Memorial is close by.

stops.name: Qutub Minar
stops.note: Stay until closing for warm light on the sandstone.

days.travel: Taxi or auto-rickshaw between stops, or the metro to the Qutub Minar (road times depend heavily on traffic — allow 30–60 minutes per leg as an estimate).
days.meals: Lunch in Connaught Place or Khan Market; try butter chicken or dal makhani for dinner.

budget.assumptions: Entry fees for the ASI monuments (Red Fort, Humayun's Tomb, Qutub Minar) change, so check them on the Archaeological Survey of India's official site. Jama Masjid, Chandni Chowk, India Gate and Bangla Sahib have no entry ticket. Accommodation, transport and meals vary too widely to estimate here.

booking.detail: Buy online on the ASI's official site to skip the ticket queue.
Book on IRCTC and check which of Delhi's five main stations your train uses.

alternatives: On a Monday, swap the days — the Red Fort is closed.
Replace the Qutub Minar with the Lotus Temple (closes earlier in winter) or Akshardham (closed Mondays, no phones).
Smoggy day? Spend more time indoors at the Red Fort museums or the National Museum.

Carry a scarf for the mosque and the gurdwara.
